title: City Funds, Street Projects, Ad Ban, Tax Collection
summary:
*   Approved an appropriation of $7,500 for city machinery and equipment.
*   Shuffled funds between accounts to bolster permanent street improvement projects.
*   Rejected a proposal to install advertising mile posts within city limits.
*   Authorized a payment of $1,340.97 to a special attorney for collecting over $8,000 in overdue taxes.
*   Defined new curb lines on 24th Street, establishing a 30-foot roadway between Rio Grande and Guadalupe streets.

Friday Sept 6th 1912.

The Council was called to order by the Mayor: Present Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen Haynes
and Powell.

Councilman Powell offered the following resolution : Curb lines
24th street
Be it resolved by the City Council of the City of Austin : That the curb lines on 24th
street from Rio Grande street to Guadalupe street be placed 15 feet from the center line
of 24th street, thus making a 30 foot roadway.

The resolution was adopted by the following vote : Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen
Haynes & Powell 3 Absent excused Councilmen Bartholomew & Hart 2

The Council then adjourned,
J. C. Robinson
City Clerk

.Be it resolved by the City Council of the City of Austin : That the sum of one thousand,
three hundred and forty dollars and ninety ($ 1,340.97 ) be and the same is hereby
appropriated out of the general contingent fund to pay commissions to J W Maxwell ,
special tax attorney for the City of Austin, for the collection of delinquent taxes
against various defendents from April 19th 1912, to August 8th 1912, as shown by the
itemized statement of services rendered in the attached bill, which is hereby made a part
of this resolution.

The amounts collected by said J W Maxwell and covered in commissions by this appropriation
were $ 8,299.14, and the exhibit covering these collections and consisting of five and a
half sheets typewriter legal cap paper , and O K'D by the signature of A P Wooldridge
Mayor, upon each sheet and part of a sheet , is attached hereto.
